messages:
Jamal: Quick sync — the proposed split that pulls 'enrichment' out of the router is sensible, but I'm worried about hotpath cross-call latency and ownership of the KV used for prefix caching. If enrichment becomes an external sync call, small requests could see tail latency regress. Anyone already measured the coupling?
Sarah: Agree — we need explicit failure modes. Option A: router returns baseline response if enrich times out. Option B: router blocks but returns a partial response when enrich completes. A feels safer for latency SLOs.
Maria: Proposed migration flow: 1) spike and perf tests, 2) run enrich in mirror mode (calls from router + no effect), 3) dual-write/catalog sync for stateful pieces, 4) gradual cutover behind feature flag. Keep the contract tiny: enrich(prefix_id) -> {enriched_fields}.
Lee: For preserving SLOs if we keep sync, we can add a tiny LRU local cache in router for last N prefixes and use batching on the enrich side to amortize token cost. Also instrument queue length.
Tomas: A couple security notes — enrichment touches derived PII for some customers. For Private deployments we must support tenant-scoped KMS keys and audit events on every enrich call. Also need a policy for masked fields vs full.
Maria: Contract suggestion: headers carry version and tenant context, e.g.

```
POST /enrich
Headers: {
  "X-Enrich-Version": "v1",
  "X-Tenant-ID": "tenant-123",
  "Authorization": "Bearer ..."
}
Body: { "prefix": "some text" }
```

Simple JSON response with fixed keys so router doesn't try to interpret arbitrary shapes.
Sarah: Observability: we must add per-call tags: enrich_latency_ms, enrich_batch_size, enrich_fallback_rate, enrich_cost_tokens. These need to flow into the Console dashboards and trigger a regression alert if tail latency > 200ms for 99th.
Jamal: For rollout safety, add these guardrails: canary at 1% for 48h, then 10% for 72h, automated rollback if fallback_rate > 1% or token cost increases by >20% vs baseline. Also need a cost cap override for low-tier customers.
Lee: Implementation note: keep the RPC interface small and transport-agnostic. Start with HTTP/gRPC adapter but design for future inproc fuse if we ever want to co-locate. That reduces long-term operational complexity.
Tomas: Who owns the migration checklist? Also need legal signoff for PII handling before canary for EU tenants.
Maria: I'll own the migration checklist and the spike. Owners: @Maria (migration + contract), @Jamal (router changes + cache), @Lee (batching + adapter). I'll draft the checklist this week.
Sarah: Add a test plan item: synthetic traffic with small/large prefixes, cold cache, and K=3 concurrent enrichers to validate queuing behavior.
Jamal: One more tiny risk — feature parity for Dedicated/Dedicated Private: ensure enrich has the same quantization/profile knobs; otherwise customers on Dedicated might see quality mismatch post-cutover.
Maria: Noted. We'll include a compatibility matrix in the spike doc.
